name: TS3A5017RGYR
title: Dual SP4T analog switch / 4:1 multiplexer-demultiplexer, 2.3 V to 3.6 V
summary: TS3A5017 holds two bidirectional single-pole four-throw switches running from one 2.3 V to 3.6 V supply. Two shared select inputs, IN1 and IN2, pick which of the four S terminals each D terminal joins, and each section has its own active-low enable. ON resistance is 11 Ω typical at 3 V, bandwidth 165 MHz, and the switch stays isolated when the supply is at 0 V.
key_figures: 11 Ω typ, 12 Ω max at 25 °C, V+ = 3 V

circuits.title: System schematic: one section selected by a controller
circuits.description: A microcontroller or other logic drives 1EN, IN1 and IN2 to choose which of 1S1 to 1S4 is joined to 1D; a fourth controller line connects to 1D, and signals pass both ways. Each control line has a resistor to ground so it sits low by default. V+ is 3.3 V with a bypass capacitor to ground. 1S1 to 1S4 go out to the rest of the system.

parts.note: pull-down on 1EN; size chosen from GPIO drive strength, power budget and switching rate

notes: With an open-drain controller output, pull-up resistors take the place of the pull-downs.
Section 2 (2EN, 2D, 2S1 to 2S4) shares IN1 and IN2 and has no connections in this circuit.

operation.text: Each of the two sections is a bidirectional SP4T switch: its D terminal connects to one of its four S terminals, chosen by IN2 and IN1, while its EN is low. EN high opens all four channels of that section. IN1 and IN2 are common to both sections.
With V+ = 0 the switch stays isolated, so signals may be present on the terminals while the part is unpowered without harming it. ISPWR(OFF) and IDPWR(OFF) give the leakage in that state.
Analog or digital signals from 0 V up to V+ pass in either direction.

IN1, IN2 and EN are always driven high or low, never left floating: at mid-threshold levels the input transistors partly conduct, which raises supply current and can leave the channel selection undefined. In the typical application the control lines are pulled down to GND by resistors; an open-drain driver uses pull-ups instead.
Unused D and S terminals may be left open or tied to GND.
V+ may be any voltage within the recommended range. Place a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor as close to the V+ pin as possible; 0.1 µF and 1 µF in parallel may be used to cover different noise frequencies.

At a square 90° corner the trace is 1.414 times wider at the apex; the change in width alters its distributed capacitance and inductance and produces a reflection. A corner cut by a 45° segment (2W across, 1W minimum inside) is better, and a rounded corner, the only form that keeps the width constant, is best.
The RGY package is soldered to a matching thermal pad on the board for thermal and mechanical performance. Vias in that pad are optional; any via under solder paste is filled, plugged or tented.

Switching times: RL = 300 Ω and CL = 35 pF on the output (CL includes probe and jig), control pulses from a 50 Ω generator with PRR ≤ 10 MHz and tr, tf < 5 ns. Bandwidth, OFF isolation and crosstalk: 50 Ω source and load, network analyzer at 0 dBm (632 mV peak-to-peak into 50 Ω) with 350 mV DC bias. THD: 600 Ω source and load, 10 µF coupling, CL = 50 pF.
TS3A5017-Q1 is the AEC-Q100 qualified automotive version.
